page: Vultr vcg-a100-96c-960g-640vram is a Dedicated Metal GPU family server configured with an x86_64 architecture Intel CPU. This bare-metal instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and a system memory capacity of 960.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 10.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Although the server name and family reference GPU capabilities, the active GPU count is reported as zero in this specific configuration.

The high memory-to-core ratio of 1:10 positions this server in the memory-optimized hardware class. This resource density is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial physical memory per execution thread without relying on GPU acceleration. The inclusion of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage, which reduces latency for disk-bound operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare-metal configuration offers high resource density, making it suitable for large-scale databases, memory-resident data processing, and enterprise application hosting. Tradeoffs include the lack of active GPU resources despite the server family classification, meaning workloads must rely entirely on the 96 dedicated Intel CPU cores for computation.
